intent: A static text segment inside a ButtonGroup, drawn as a filled plate with the same hairline as the controls beside it.
typical_uses: A caption or unit joined to the controls around it (a prefix, a currency sign)

dont_use_when.situation: A caption that names a form control, outside any ButtonGroup
Text or a unit attached inside one text field

invariants.text: Any svg inside the segment, at any depth, is sized to the small icon size, does not shrink, and ignores pointer events.

anti_patterns.dont: Put an interactive control inside ButtonGroupText
anti_patterns.do_instead: Place the control as its own direct child of the ButtonGroup; the text segment is a static plate, not a container for controls

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: useRender's render prop takes an element or a function of the text segment's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

good.title: A caption joined to the actions it introduces
good.code:
<ButtonGroup aria-label="Sort order">
  <ButtonGroupText>Sort</ButtonGroupText>
  <Button variant="outline">Newest first</Button>
  <Button variant="outline">Oldest first</Button>
</ButtonGroup>

bad.title: A button placed inside the text segment
bad.why: The Button is not a direct child of the group, so it is not joined, and it sits inside a muted plate meant for static text.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, {}> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. useRender's render prop takes an element or a function of the text segment's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.
